headline: Nvidia opens internal probe into Jensen Huang
dek: The board is investigating after pressure from Congress, per CNBC.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Congress pushes
body: US lawmakers want an investigation into Jensen Huang's ties to an alleged Chinese agent, per CNBC, TechCrunch and The Verge.
Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation into the matter.

points.t: A memo says executive Alice Huang was recruited.
To gather chip data and push for easier exports.
The two Huangs are not related (The Verge).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Nvidia's defense
body: Nvidia denies wrongdoing and says contacts were normal customer meetings, per TechCrunch and CNBC.
The company says it does not share classified information.

items.t: House panels want a closed session on November 18 (CNBC).
The ask comes a day after quarterly earnings (CNBC).
A separate New Matrix case also draws fire (CNBC).

caption.hook: Nvidia's board opened an internal probe into Jensen Huang after pressure from Congress.
body: Per CNBC, three House committee chairs asked Huang for a closed-door briefing on November 18, a day after third-quarter earnings. TechCrunch and The Verge report that a US intelligence memo, first reported by The New York Times, alleges China recruited executive Alice Huang to get close to the CEO and gather information about AI chips.

Nvidia denies wrongdoing. A spokesperson said contacts with Alice Huang were not unusual and that the company does not share classified information with customers. Alice Huang is an executive at Megaspeed, a Nvidia customer, and the two are not related. The claims are unproven.
caption.cta: Should chip makers face stricter oversight over China?
